title: Vana: exile
hook: Bhima wants to fight now, and Yudhishthira holds to the word he gave in the hall

segments.voice: Yesterday: Vana, the forest, and the great argument. Draupadi asked for might, Yudhishthira for forgiveness. Your line was a time for strength, or to let go.

Bhima has been listening, and he's done waiting. He's built for action, strong and impatient. He's watched his brothers live on roots and his wife sleep on the ground, and he can't see the point. Our enemies cheated, he says. Why are we keeping faith with cheats? Let's go back and take what's ours. It's a fair question, and he asks it loudly.
screen: `BHIMA IS DONE WAITING.` → `WHY KEEP FAITH WITH CHEATS?` → `THE BROTHER WHO GAVE HIS WORD.`

segments.voice: Bhima's case is strong, and the epic lets him make it in full. The game was a trap. Time is passing, and every day in the forest their enemies grow stronger. A warrior who sits still, he says, is failing at his own duty. Yudhishthira hears him out, then answers with one thing. I gave my word. In the hall, in front of everyone, he agreed to the terms of the last throw: the years in the forest, then a year in hiding. Breaking that promise now, he says, would be worse to him than losing the kingdom. The old word for what he's holding on to is satya: truth, and also truthfulness, being someone whose word holds. Then he adds something more practical, and more honest. Even if they wanted to fight now, look who stands on the other side: Bhishma, Drona, Karna, great warriors all. We aren't ready. So the forest isn't only a punishment to be endured. It's time: time to keep a promise, and time to prepare. Bhima's frustration isn't wrong, and the epic doesn't mock it. But Yudhishthira's refusal isn't weakness either. It's a man deciding that who he is matters more than how fast he gets his kingdom back. A stubborn sense of what he owes walked him back to the dice board when the old king summoned him. Here, it keeps four brothers and a wife waiting with him under the trees.
screen: `BHIMA: WHY WAIT?` · `YUDHISHTHIRA: I GAVE MY WORD.` · `SATYA: A WORD THAT HOLDS.` · then, large: `THE FOREST IS ALSO TIME.`

segments.voice: Think of a promise you're keeping that turned out harder than you expected: a commitment, a job, a way you said you'd treat someone. Let the Bhima in you ask, why not drop it, and breathe; then let the Yudhishthira in you ask, who would I be if I did, and breathe again. Nothing needs deciding now; if you pray, you can hold that promise in your prayer.
Vana. The forest of exile, where Bhima wants to fight now and Yudhishthira keeps the word he gave in the hall.
Your line: keep the word you gave. For Yudhishthira, a word that holds was worth more than a kingdom. Day seven hundred eighty, done.

howItsDone: Yudhishthira's insistence on keeping his word in exile is held up in Hindu storytelling as a picture of satya, truthfulness, and is discussed alongside Bhima's very different temperament.

chat.says: They were cheated. Why didn't Yudhishthira just go back and fight?
options: He'd given his word to the terms, and they weren't ready for Bhishma, Drona and Karna.
He was afraid of Bhima's temper and only wanted to calm his brother down.
He believed the dice game was fair, so they had lost the kingdom honestly.
chat.meaning: In the hall Yudhishthira accepted the terms: the forest years, then a year hidden. And he knew Bhishma, Drona and Karna stood on the other side.

Bhima.meaning: the second Pandava brother, famous for strength and temper

satya.meaning: truth, and truthfulness: a word that holds

Bhishma.meaning: great-uncle of both families, a mighty warrior

Karna.meaning: a great archer on the Kauravas' side

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Aranyaka Parva), Bhima's appeal to Yudhishthira and Yudhishthira's reply (the promise made at the dice game; the strength of Bhishma, Drona and Karna)

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli that Yudhishthira says keeping his promise matters more to him than the kingdom (or life, or immortality) and the wording.
Confirm Yudhishthira names Bhishma, Drona and Karna (and others) as reasons they are not ready; this leads into Vyasa's arrival.
Bhima as 'strong, hungry, impatient' is characterization drawn from the epic's portrait; Keeper may prefer softer wording.
The terms of exile (forest years then a year in hiding) are stated without numbers under the claims rule.
Original: satya is offered as the concept at stake; the script doesn't claim Yudhishthira uses this exact word here.

Editor: cut the superlative 'of all the brothers, he's the one built for action' and the 'hungry' label; replaced the closing 'both what ruined him and what he refuses to give up' (the same virtue-and-disaster move as day 769) with a concrete line about the habit that brought him back to the board.
